Package neqsim.process.processmodel

Class RunStatus

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.processmodel.RunStatus
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class RunStatus extends Object implements Serializable
Structured outcome of the most recent run of a ProcessSystem or ProcessModel.

A RunStatus answers the question "did the last run succeed, and if not, which unit failed and why?" without forcing the caller to catch and parse a RuntimeException. It records a per-unit outcome list and, on failure, the first failed unit's name and error message.

The recorder methods (reset(), recordSuccess(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), recordFailure(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String), markComplete(boolean)) are intended to be driven by the owning process during a run; the accessor methods and toJson() are intended for agents and reporting.

Version:
1.0
Author:
NeqSim

      public void recordSuccess(String unitName, String unitType, String areaName)

    • recordSuccess

      void recordSuccess(UnitRunStatus unitStatus)
      Records a previously created immutable success status.

      Package-private for ProcessSystem, which can safely reuse success records while its unit structure and names are unchanged. Failure records are never reused because their error text belongs to one particular run.

      Parameters:
      unitStatus - immutable successful unit status

    • recordFailure

      public void recordFailure(String unitName, String unitType, String errorMessage)
      Records that a unit failed to run. The first recorded failure is reported as the run's failed unit.
      Parameters:
      unitName - the unit operation name
      unitType - the unit operation type (simple class name), or null if unknown
      errorMessage - the error message describing the failure

    • recordFailure

      public void recordFailure(String unitName, String unitType, String errorMessage, String areaName)

    • markComplete

      public void markComplete(boolean overallSuccess)
      Marks the run as complete with the given overall outcome. A run is considered successful only if the supplied flag is true and no unit failure was recorded.
